title: Disarm, do not escalate
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Does turning up the volume ever help?
A student said: it is all about disarming people and being on their side, not on opposite sides, and elevating the conversation to be more and more aggressive does the complete opposite.
Another said that you lower their guard with a first statement that shows their credibility in one sentence.
Jose said that they are building the empathy, which gives the momentum, and then they use the tools: how do I get you that money?
He said that complexity, with many people and many sheets of numbers, is what tires us, and then the person quits and you start again and train them again.
He said that he likes to watch how people manage themselves under conflict, and that one example is a psychological test given to a young person that tells you nothing about who they are.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what disarming would have been.
Write the credibility line you would open with.
Write the tool you would use after empathy.
Write how you will keep complexity from tiring you.

check.q: What did a student say escalating does?
What did Jose say empathy gives?
What does a first credible statement do?

recap: Disarm first. Use empathy for momentum.
